final OSCE Learning points "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPRE FINAL OSCE LEARNING POINTS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E05\/12 \/23\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOSCE QUESTIONS :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;1) Dialysis Disequilibrium syndrome?\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome (DDS)\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;refers to an array of neurological\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;manifestations seen during or following\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;dialysis, primarily after the new initiation\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;of dialysis.However, it can also be seen in\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;chronic dialysis patients who miss their\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;regular dialysis treatments. This\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;syndrome is thought to arise from fluid\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;shifts during hemodialysis, causing\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;cerebral edema and a wide variety of\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;neurological symptoms. In continuous\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;renal replacement therapies (CRRT),\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;where fluid shift is limited, dialysis\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;disequilibrium syndrome is rarely\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;reported.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe common risk factors that predispose a patient to dialysis dysequilibrium syndrome are\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFirst hemodialysis treatment\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHigh blood urea nitrogen (BUN) (above 175 mg\/dL or 60 mmol\/L) before initiation of dialysis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EExtremes of age – children and elderly\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESudden change in dialysis regimen\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPre-existing neurological diseases such as stroke, malignant hypertension, head trauma, or seizure disorder\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPresence of other conditions causing cerebral edema (hyponatremia, hepatic encephalopathy)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EConditions causing increased permeability of the blood-brain barrier (sepsis, meningitis, encephalitis, hemolytic uremic syndrome, vasculitis)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;2)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;How spironolactone cause\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;gynecomastea?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Spironolactone induces gynecomastia by\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;decreasing testosterone production,\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;increasing peripheral conversion of\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;testosterone to estradiol, and displacing\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;estradiol from sex hormone-binding\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;globulin.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELearning points :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHow to approach the patient and take detailed history and link the past history with the present illness.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt about the Dialysis Disequilibrium syndrome\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHow spironolactone cause the "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4-dec-2023\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E60 YEAR OLD MALE CKD ON MAINTENANCE HEMODIALYSIS WITH ANEMIA OF CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE WITH HYPERTENSION\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003EThis is an a online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 60 year old male, who is a resident of Nalgonda ,farmer by occupation came with\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EChief complaints :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPedal edema since 3 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EShortness of breath since 20 days. Decreased urine output since 15 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHistory of presenting illness:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 3 months back when he noticed bilateral pedal edema initially extending to ankle Gradually progressed up to thighs which worsened during last 15 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDecreased urine output since 15 days, not associated with frequency, urgency burning micturation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGrade 3 shortness of breath, no aggravating and relieving factors.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBefore the presenting illness :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient had History of trauma by fall from tree 17 years back, where he used NSAIDS for 4\/5 yrs ..\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThen 12 years back he developed pedal edema where He got diagnosed that he had kidney problem and he was on medication and where edema was subsided and it was more recurrent on those 5 years.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThen he was diagnosed with CKD For which he got treated by dailysis initially and then he started using medications\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient was apparently well till 3 months\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;back\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;3 months back patient developed\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;bilateral\u0026nbsp; pedal edema, facial puffiness\u0026nbsp; for\u0026nbsp; the first time and shortness of breath\u0026nbsp; so he visited local hospital and they\u0026nbsp; referred to our hospital for dailysis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESince then patient was coming here regularly twice a weak for dialysis .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter his last dialysis session he went back home and he developed discomfort in chest and weakness of limbs . Patient also had few episodes of altered sensorium in between.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESo he was brought to hospital again.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EKnown case of hypertension since 6 months\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo history of diabetes mellitus, asthma, cardiovascular disease , epilepsy, tuberculosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere is a history of blood transfusions.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMixed diet\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESleep adequate\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBowel-Regular\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBladder-Irregular\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo known allergies\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Econsumes alcohol occasionally\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESmokes tobacco\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDAILY ROUTINE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBefore 3 years :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWakes up at 5 am and goes to field and toddy trees\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBreakfast at 9 am -rice\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfternoon- lunch 12 pm\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEvening drinks toddy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd dinner by 9 pm and
